scenes.desc: Nacida en el círculo del GRM y bautizada por Pierre Henry: sustituye los sonidos concretos por otros sintetizados electrónicamente. François Bayle acuña en 1974 «música acusmática»: una música que se genera en un estudio y se proyecta en una sala, como el cine.

scenes.name: Cecil Taylor
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: El reverso de Coleman: formación de conservatorio (New England Conservatory), Stravinsky y Bartók junto a Ellington, Monk, Waller o Brubeck, y una música más densa, atomista, percusiva y sin romanticismo. Su estilo está formado hacia 1954, antes del free: disonancias, líneas fragmentadas, ataque de martillo neumático, primero sobre standards (Transition, Newport, el Five Spot), luego cada vez más libre en Candid («Cell Walk for Celeste», «como si Charles Ives se bajara en la calle 125») y en Blue Note con Unit Structures y Conquistador! (1966). Trabaja de lavaplatos mientras gana premios; en los setenta se convierte en veterano becado y patrocinado, con conciertos de piano solo como exhibiciones atléticas, música para Baryshnikov y Alvin Ailey y la caja Berlin '88.

scenes.name: Voces del jazz moderno: Ella, Sarah, Carmen y el vocalese
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: La faceta más ligada a la tradición del jazz de los setenta y ochenta. Norman Granz convierte a Ella Fitzgerald, ya superventas desde la banda de Chick Webb, en una artista mayor con los songbooks dedicados a Porter, Gershwin, Arlen, Ellington y Berlin y los directos de Berlín y Roma; en Pablo la empareja con Basie o Joe Pass. Carmen McRae y Betty Carter prolongan a Billie Holiday con libertades rítmicas casi vanguardistas; Sheila Jordan y Mel Tormé siguen sus propios caminos. El vocalese de Eddie Jefferson y Jon Hendricks pone letra a solos famosos y convierte al cantante en un griot que narra la historia del jazz (Joni Mitchell con «Goodbye Pork Pie Hat», Manhattan Transfer). Bobby McFerrin, imitador de metales y director de orquesta, triunfa con «Don't Worry, Be Happy» y se niega a explotar el éxito.

scenes.name: Big bands de repertorio y orquestas contemporáneas
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Desde los cincuenta la big band sobrevive como formación ocasional, banda de ciudad o grupo de repertorio. Sauter y Finegan experimentan con instrumentos raros; Don Ellis, Maynard Ferguson y Buddy Rich se acercan al rock y a los compases extraños. La Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra toca los lunes en el Village Vanguard desde 1966 por diecisiete dólares y sobrevive a sus fundadores como Vanguard Jazz Orchestra. La big band de Toshiko Akiyoshi (pianista a lo Powell, raíces japonesas, diecisiete instrumentos de viento) y Lew Tabackin domina la costa oeste en los setenta. Gil Evans y su heredera Maria Schneider mantienen la devoción por la orquesta; el Smithsonian, el Lincoln Center y las escuelas convierten la big band en pedagogía histórica, como la orquesta sinfónica.

scenes.name: Sonny Rollins
scenes.book: Historia del jazz
scenes.desc: Frente a las «capas de sonido» de Coltrane, Rollins define el sonido clásico del tenor de la época desde el corazón de la tradición: «que se oiga lo antiguo y lo nuevo». Criado entre Monk, Bud Powell, Parker y Miles, pasa por el quinteto Brown-Roach y mide fuerzas con Coltrane en Tenor Madness. Celebra la improvisación pura, con cadenzas a capela que mezclan arias y canciones pop, un repertorio que va de Kurt Weill a «I'm an Old Cowhand» y temas «para soplar» convertidos en standards («St. Thomas», «Oleo», «Doxy»). Schuller analiza su desarrollo temático, motivo a motivo. Saxophone Colossus, Way Out West en trío sin piano, el Village Vanguard y la Freedom Suite culminan en 1956-1958; luego se retira a practicar en el puente de Williamsburg y vuelve con The Bridge, entre experimentos y regresos a lo conocido.

scenes.name: Antonio, Rosario, Pilar López y las grandes compañías
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La época de las parejas y los ballets. Antonio Ruiz Soler (1921-1990) bailó con Rosario de 1928 a 1952, con películas en Hollywood y giras por América, y luego se dedicó a la coreografía (El amor brujo, el martinete con yunque); Rosario, discípula del maestro Realito, acabó en la enseñanza. Pilar López, hermana de la Argentinita, formó en su ballet a Farruco, Gades y Mario Maya y añadió los palillos a la siguiriya. El Farruco (1936-1997), autodidacta, fue el patriarca del baile gitano de hombre (Bodas de gloria). El Güito, el más ortodoxo, ganó en 1959 el premio Sarah Bernhardt de París frente a Nureyev. Mario Maya renovó la escena con Camelamos naquerar (1976), con Concha Vargas. Matilde Coral, heredera de Pastora Imperio, maestra de Milagros Menjíbar y María Pagés; Manuela Vargas, «la dama del flamenco»; Tía Juana la del Pipa, que no fue profesional hasta los cuarenta; la Chunga, que bailaba descalza; y Manuela Carrasco, la más importante de su generación, completan el retrato, con las escuelas de Granada (Manolete, Mariquilla) y Córdoba (Concha Calero).

scenes.name: El piano flamenco
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Lorca tocó el piano para la Argentinita y Caracol lo usó en lugar de la guitarra, pero el piano flamenco tiene sus propios nombres. Arturo Pavón (1930), de la familia de los Pavón y de Caracol, formado en el conservatorio, hizo dúo con Luisa Ortega en el tablao Los Canasteros; Pepe Romero (1936-1997) fue el pianista ortodoxo e investigador; Felipe Campuzano, compositor de Andalucía espiritual. Chano Domínguez (1960) viene del jazz y lo une al flamenco; Dorantes (1969), de los Peña de Lebrija, estudió en el conservatorio y Yehudi Menuhin lo llevó a Mont de Marsan; Diego Gallego, de la escuela de Campuzano, ha tocado con Rancapino y Maíta Vende Cá.

scenes.name: El arte jondo: duende y universalidad
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La tesis de partida: el flamenco, tal como hoy se conoce, tiene poco más de un siglo, pero ha pasado de un desahogo de la Andalucía oprimida, transmitido de generación en generación y disfrutado por unos pocos en reuniones, a un arte mayor aplaudido en los teatros de todo el mundo. La bailaora Cristina Hoyos, en el prólogo, defiende que siga evolucionando con fusiones y mestizajes siempre que no pierda su raíz. Arbelos reúne elogios de voces muy distintas: Manuel de Falla («no hay música más rica, ni más viva en toda Europa»), Stravinski en 1921 («un arte de composición»), Miles Davis en 1950 («es como nuestro blues»), Chick Corea, Unamuno, Pemán, Rubén Darío, Lorca, Juan Ramón Jiménez o Jean Cocteau. Su intemporalidad y universalidad lo ponen a la altura de los clásicos, aunque su cuna sea popular y anónimos sus primeros cultores. Y lo que conmueve al público sin conocimientos previos es el duende: la corriente indefinible que une al intérprete con quien lo escucha. El libro quiere ser una guía sencilla y didáctica para entender lo que se oye en un recital.

scenes.name: Las dinastías de Jerez
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La ciudad de las bulerías y de las grandes familias gitanas. El Gloria (1893-1954) cantaba saetas y bulerías y creó sus villancicos. Agujeta el Viejo transmitió los cantes de Manuel Torre, y su hijo el Agujetas (1939) tiene la voz rota de los «sonidos negros» de Lorca. Terremoto (1934-1981) fue indispensable en los festivales de los sesenta por siguiriyas y bulerías; el Sordera (1927-2001) brilló en los tablaos de Madrid y dejó una dinastía; el Chocolate (1931), voz de la escuela de Torre, ganó el Giraldillo de la Bienal de 1986 y un Grammy Latino en 2002. Tío Juane cantaba martinetes forjando una herradura y la Paquera (1934) tenía una voz de enorme potencia. José Mercé (1955), de la dinastía de Paco la Luz y cantaor de la compañía de Gades, es a comienzos del siglo XXI el cantaor de más éxito, por unir la raíz jonda con la música de su tiempo. Siguen el Capullo, maestro del compás, Diego Carrasco, cuyo ritmo buscan Camarón o Morente, y la Macanita, la gran cantaora joven de Jerez.

scenes.name: Las bamberas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante que acompañaba el vaivén del columpio, la bamba, en las fiestas campesinas al acabar la cosecha o en las fiestas patronales, con ritmo de soleá lenta. Como todos los cantes folclóricos andaluces que se aflamencaron entre finales del XIX y la primera mitad del XX, su jondura depende del intérprete: unas sevillanas de Camarón son flamencas; las de un coro rociero, canción folclórica. Su creadora indiscutible fue la Niña de los Peines, y Camarón cantó por bamberas «La leyenda del tiempo» de Lorca.

scenes.name: La rumba
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante de ida y vuelta más estudiado, tan parecido al tango que confunde a los investigadores. Según Papa Wemba su melodía es centroafricana, de Zaire: viajó con la trata de esclavos a Cuba y de allí a España. La aportación más flamenca fue la de Pepe de la Matrona, que vivió en Cuba a mediados de la década de 1910 (Recuerdos de La Habana, 1914). La rumba catalana tiene su estilo propio, con el Pescaílla, marido de Lola Flores, y Peret, y su toque rapidísimo «del ventilador». Poco apreciada por los flamencos, ha crecido con la salsa entre el público joven; Paco de Lucía tuvo su primer gran éxito con la rumba «Entre dos aguas» y la «Macarena» de Los del Río batió todos los récords. Su baile es sensual y provocador.

scenes.name: La escuela gaditana
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Los cantaores de Cádiz, herederos del Mellizo, dueños de las cantiñas, los tanguillos y las alegrías. Aurelio Sellés (1887-1974) fue uno de sus puntales y dominó cantiñas, siguiriyas, soleares y malagueñas. Pericón de Cádiz (1901-1980) contó su vida en Las mil y una historias de Pericón. La Perla de Cádiz (1925-1975) recreó los estilos de su tierra. Chano Lobato (1927) es el «dueño del compás»: acompañó a Antonio, Matilde Coral y Manuela Vargas y desde los ochenta canta como solista. Les siguen Rancapino, continuador de Aurelio; Chaquetón, de la saga de los Chaqueta y en la línea del Mellizo; Mariana Cornejo, popular por un anuncio cantado por tanguillos; y Juanito Villar, salido de las comparsas de carnaval, que grabó con Paco Cepero.

scenes.name: Villancicos y zambombas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes navideños sobre el nacimiento del «Niño Manuel», de remoto origen profano (hay quien los deriva del zéjel árabe), que el legendario Niño Gloria de Jerez adaptó al compás de bulerías, tangos y tanguillos; sus villancicos los conocen todos los artistas. José Mercé los recreó con gran jondura en la serie Así canta nuestra tierra por Navidad (doce volúmenes), con el tocaor Parrilla de Jerez y el aula de folclore de la Cátedra de Flamencología. En Jerez se celebran por Navidad las zambombas: reuniones familiares en patios de vecinos o bodegas donde se canta en corro por bulerías y tangos, se baila en el centro y se comen pestiños.

scenes.name: Las bulerías
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: El cante festero por excelencia, con el compás de la soleá mucho más acelerado; nacido a comienzos del siglo XX (Mairena atribuye al Loco Mateo, en el XIX, el remate acelerado de las soleares). Tiene dos centros: Cádiz, más larga y suave, y Jerez, más corta y bulliciosa, «la ciudad de los gitanos» de Lorca, donde hasta las piedras cantan por bulerías y el soniquete se lleva en la sangre. El nombre se discute: burla, bolero o bulla. Su métrica lo admite todo, coplas de soleá, seguidillas o canciones (en Utrera, letras de canciones ajenas): un buen cantaor podría cantar por bulerías la guía telefónica. Cierra cualquier festival en el fin de fiesta, y quien la domina en el cante, el baile o el toque domina todo el flamenco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de ida y vuelta: colombiana, guajira, vidalita, milonga
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes folclóricos hispanoamericanos (rumba, milonga, colombiana, guajira, vidalita) aflamencados por la manera de cantarlos en Andalucía; fáciles de cantar, no se consideran cante jondo. Llegaron en la última década del XIX y se difundieron desde los años treinta: son la última gran incorporación al flamenco. La idea de que eran cantes andaluces que fueron a América y volvieron es pura mitopoética. Sabicas contaba que él y Vicente Escudero, con muchos contratos en América y el repertorio flamenco agotado, empezaron a tocar esas canciones «con este aire nuestro». La colombiana no viene de América: la creó Pepe Marchena en los treinta, con enorme éxito; Carmen Amaya fue la primera en cantarla y bailarla, Sabicas la tocaba sin nombrarla por vergüenza y Juanito Valderrama popularizó la suya en los cincuenta. La guajira, de Cuba, fue la primera en llegar y la que mejor se adaptó (en Cádiz se cantaban «guajiras festeras» por bulerías); sus coplas son décimas. La vidalita, del norte argentino y triste, la recuperaron en los noventa jóvenes como Mayte Martín; la milonga pampeana la trajo Pepa Oro en compás de tangos, Chacón la remataba por tanguillos y Pepe de la Matrona la grabó. Hay dos discos fundamentales: Cantes de ida y vuelta (Junta de Andalucía, 1985, con Menese, José Mercé y Luis de Córdoba) y Dos mundos cantan (Expo 92, con Valderrama, Rocío Jurado y Chano Lobato).

scenes.name: Las saetas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cante dolido que solo se canta en Semana Santa, al paso de las imágenes, a palo seco o con cornetas y tambores, por martinetes, siguiriyas (las más comunes), soleares, cañas o polos, con coplas de exaltación religiosa que exigen gran potencia de voz. Nace a finales del XIX en Cádiz: Enrique el Mellizo y sus hijos detenían al Nazareno desde los cuatro balcones de su casa con sus saetas. A él se atribuye la saeta por siguiriyas, que desarrolló Manuel Centeno en el siglo XX. Manuel Torre, el Niño Gloria, la Niña de los Peines, Manolo Caracol y Antonio Mairena eran esperados en Semana Santa para cantarlas sin amplificación desde un balcón a la altura de las imágenes; Manuel Mairena grabó un vía crucis entero. Un equipo francés grabó en directo a los saeteros de Jerez, Arcos y Lebrija en la Semana Santa de 1993 para la colección Flamenco vivo.

scenes.name: Demófilo y los Machado
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Antonio Machado y Álvarez, Demófilo, fue el primer autor español que dedicó un libro entero al flamenco: la Colección de cantes flamencos recogidos y anotados (1881), piedra angular de la flamencología moderna; escribió también sobre las saetas y dirigió la revista El Folclore Andaluz (1882-1883). Sus hijos, los poetas Antonio y Manuel Machado (autor de Cante hondo), heredaron la afición, y sus coplas se cantan a menudo sin que los cantaores sepan que son versos cultos. Calixto Sánchez dedicó a Antonio Machado un disco en 2001, y José Menese hizo suyas las letras de Francisco Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: La farruca y el garrotín
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes aflamencados de fuera de Andalucía. La farruca, gallega, llegó a Cádiz con los comerciantes gallegos del XIX y es más baile que cante; la popularizó Manuel Torre a principios del XX y hoy casi solo la canta Pepe Menese, con una letra de Moreno Galván que se hizo himno en la Transición. Su baile, viril, lo creó Faíco; Carmen Amaya lo bailó vestida de hombre, Falla lo incluyó en El sombrero de tres picos y la versión de Antonio Gades en la película de Los Tarantos, la última de Carmen Amaya, se enseña hoy en las academias. El garrotín viene del folclore asturiano y lo hicieron suyo los gitanos de Lleida; lo difundieron Carmen Amaya y la Niña de los Peines, que lo cantaba con aire de tangos, Faíco hizo sus coreografías y Blas Vega recogió una copla antigua cantada por el Chaparro en la Magna antología del cante flamenco.

scenes.name: Los fandangos de Huelva
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Huelva reclama la cuna del fandango andaluz y es la provincia con más estilos: las antologías recogen más de treinta y cinco, locales (Encinasola, el Alosno, Cabezas Rubias, Calañas, el Andévalo, Valverde del Camino) y personales, creados por profesionales como Paco Isidro, Pepe Rebollo, el Comía, Antonio Rengel, Pérez de Guzmán y Paco Toronjo; de fuera dejaron su sello el Gloria, Macandé, el Carbonerillo y Manolo Caracol. Paco Toronjo, fijo en los festivales desde finales de los sesenta y en las bienales de Sevilla, les dio una jondura difícil de imitar. El baile, de pareja y galanteo, se ve ya poco.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Levante o de las minas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacidos del trabajo en las minas del siglo XIX en las sierras de Cartagena y La Unión y en Linares, La Carolina y Andújar: cantes de dolor profundo sobre la mina, sus accidentes y los compañeros muertos, hechos con fandangos regionales, murcianas, malagueñas y el cante de madrugá de los mineros. La taranta, el más significativo, tiene dos estilos, el de Linares (Gabriel Moreno, Carmen Linares) y el de La Unión (Encarnación Fernández, Pepe Cros), y Camarón le puso dulzura; el taranto, almeriense, tiene compás porque nació para el baile de Carmen Amaya en los cuarenta, con el Ciego de la Playa y Pedro el Morato. La cartagenera, de temas más urbanos, la fijó Antonio Chacón a finales del XIX y la cantaron Cayetano Muriel, Manuel Centeno, Manuel Torre y la Niña de los Peines. La minera se atribuye a Rojo el Alpargatero, Antonio Grau Mora, que hacia 1885 abrió en La Unión una posada que acabó en café cantante y oía cantar a los mineros de madrugada: es el gran creador de los cantes mineros. Las granaínas, de Frasquito Yerbabuena y sobre todo Chacón, son un cante casi barroco hoy cargado de vibratos operísticos. Sin minas, los concursos de Linares y La Unión mantienen vivos estos cantes.

scenes.name: Las cantiñas: alegrías, caracoles, mirabrás y romeras
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes alegres de la bahía de Cádiz, en compás de soleá y muy ligados al baile, que arranca majestuoso y va ganando fuerza hasta desplantes electrizantes. Nacen probablemente de la jotilla gaditana, hermanada con la jota aragonesa por la resistencia común contra Napoleón, de ahí las letras sobre la guerra y el mar; la leyenda atribuye su creación a Enrique el Mellizo, que oyó a una muchacha cantar jotas con un ciego. Tomaron identidad en la segunda mitad del XIX. Hay cantiñas del Pinini de Utrera y Lebrija y de Córdoba; la rosa ya no se canta. Las alegrías, al principio baile de mujer sola, se hicieron más lentas a comienzos del XX y empiezan con el «tirititrán» que, según Chano Lobato, inventó Pericón de Cádiz al olvidar la letra; las cantaron el Mellizo, Ignacio Ezpeleta, Aurelio Sellés, Manolo Vargas y Pericón. Los caracoles, de Tío José el Granaíno (picador del Chiclanero), los recreó Chacón y triunfaron en Madrid («la gran calle de Alcalá»). El mirabrás son alegrías largas (José Menese, con letras de Moreno Galván), y las romeras se atribuyen al Granaíno o a una cantaora llamada la Romera. Hoy el gran intérprete es Chano Lobato.

scenes.name: Los tangos, tientos y marianas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Con bulerías y cantiñas, el gran cante festero: letras de vida, amor y muerte con cierta ligereza, ritmo vivo y pegadizo fácil de seguir con palmas, y un baile sensual. Cádiz y Sevilla se disputan su paternidad, pero los hay en toda Andalucía y en Extremadura; Triana tiene el estilo del Titi y Jerez su propio sello. Su origen musical se discute: Mairena los tenía por cante básico gitano; los estudios recientes los llevan a Cuba y las habaneras llegadas a Sevilla y Cádiz en la segunda mitad del XIX; los granadinos defienden una raíz morisca (el disco Granada canta por tangos recoge trece estilos, entre ellos los de la morería). Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Creation of Bowie Bonds (1997)
facts.body: In 1997, David Bowie, in collaboration with investment banker David Pullman, created a financial instrument called "Bowie Bonds." This involved securitizing 287 songs from 25 albums recorded before 1990, effectively making them asset-backed securities. In exchange for forfeiting 10 years of royalty income, Bowie received an immediate lump sum payment of $55 million. He utilized this money to repurchase the rights to songs he had lost to his former manager, Tony DeFrees. "David Bowie and an investment banker named David Pullman created a financial instrument called Bowie Bonds. To use Wall Street speak, 287 songs from 25 albums recorded before 1990 became asset-backed securities. In exchange for forfeiting royalty income for a period of 10 years, Bowie received an immediate payment of $55 million. He used that money to buy out the rights to songs he lost to his former manager, Tony DeFrees."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Bowie Net (1997-2006) – Pioneering ISP
facts.body: Over a couple of years, Bowie and a small team created Bowie Net, launched around 1997-1998, which functioned as an internet service provider. Subscribers paid $20 a month for internet access and a @DavidBowie.com email address, or $6 for access to exclusive content like songs, music videos, chat rooms, images of his paintings, and journal writings. Bowie was known to lurk anonymously in chat rooms. In 1999, it held a song contest with 80,000 lyric submissions, won by Alex Grant whose lyrics appeared on the *Hours* album. It featured LiveAndWell.com for live tracks and Bowie World, a 3D virtual environment where users could navigate a Bowie-themed city as avatars and communicate with other fans. At its peak in 1999, Bowie Net had 100,000 customers but ceased operations in 2006 as larger companies copied his innovations. "Bowie Net was incredibly ahead of its time."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Bowie Bonds (1997) – Financial Innovation
facts.body: In 1997, Bowie, with banker David Pullman, pioneered "Bowie Bonds," a financial instrument where he securitized his future music royalties as collateral to issue bonds. He sold these bonds, raising $55 million, which he then used to repurchase the rights to his music that he had lost through previous bad management deals with Tony DeFries. This marked the first time a performer used their cash flow potential in this manner. Issued a few years before widespread music piracy, the bonds initially had a high A3 rating and paid 7.9% interest over 10 years, attracting Prudential Insurance. However, within 18 months, the music industry tanked due to Napster and declining physical sales, causing the bonds' rating to drop to BAA3 (near junk status). In 2007, the bonds were liquidated, and all music rights reverted to Bowie, meaning by his death in 2016, he owned almost everything he had produced. "This was the first time in financial history that a performer had used their cash flow potential to make money."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: 50th Birthday Concert (1997)
facts.body: Bowie celebrated his 50th birthday by throwing a concert at Madison Square Garden, joined on stage by prominent alt-rockers such as Sonic Youth, Foo Fighters, The Cure's Robert Smith, and Lou Reed, demonstrating his continued relevance and connections within the alternative music scene, even if his 50s became his quietest artistic period. "Earthling arrived just a few weeks after a 50th birthday concert Bowie threw himself at Madison Square Garden joined on stage by such alt rockers as Sonic Youth, Foo Fighters, The Cures Robert Smith and Old Friend and Alt Rock Godfather Lou Reed."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Be Here Now Recording Sessions (1997)
facts.body: The recording sessions for the third album, *Be Here Now*, in 1997 were a period of constant, low-level fighting between Noel and Liam. The band was burned out and heavily under the influence of cocaine, which Noel later believed affected the album's sound and led to decisions like layering excessive guitars and turning up the high end. "Meanwhile, Noel and Liam were constantly fighting throughout the whole thing."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Be Here Now Recording – Constant Low-Level Fighting (1997)
facts.body: During the recording sessions for their third album, "Be Here Now," Noel and Liam were in a constant state of low-level conflict. While there were no dramatic "giant blowups," those present described it as a persistent, unyielding tension, like a "long low-level seizure," exacerbated by widespread cocaine use. "There were no giant blowups, but those who were there say it was like one of those long low-level seizures that just did not let up."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Struggle to Exit Britpop (Post-1997)
facts.body: Following the peak of Britpop, Oasis found it challenging to transition out of the movement, facing difficulties similar to those experienced by Suede. Despite the commercial success of albums like "Be Here Now," their adherence to a purist Britpop sound became less relevant by late 1997, complicating their adaptation to the emerging post-Britpop landscape. "fue de las bandas que más les costó salir de movimiento gripo."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.name: Oasis

facts.title: Mexican Secret Service Incident – December 3, 1997, Foro Sol Stadium, Mexico City, Security Chief Run Over
facts.body: After playing a 25-song set at Foro Sol Stadium in Mexico City on December 3, 1997, U2 were approached backstage with an urgent request to leave immediately. Three sons of Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo had arrived unannounced without tickets; venue security had waved them and their secret service detail through in a van. When the president's sons and their bodyguards tried to exit through a restricted backstage camera crane area — dangerous due to counterweights — a camera operator told them to leave, causing a confrontation. U2's road crew intervened, not knowing who the group was. Jerry Mele, U2's head of security, placed himself in front of the van to detain it pending police arrival; the van drove over him, resulting in serious back injuries from which he never fully recovered. The next day, U2 were summoned to the president's palace where the sons produced albums for signing. President Zedillo asked that the incident be kept quiet, stating it could have been much worse. "So what could U2 do?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Incident with Mexican President's Sons (1997)
facts.body: On December 3, 1997, after a concert in Mexico City, U2's backstage area was invaded by the unannounced, ticketless sons of Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo and their secret service. When the secret service attempted to take a shortcut through a dangerous, off-limits camera crane area, U2's head of security, Jerry Mele, was run over by their van, sustaining serious back injuries. "The van just ran over Jerry, resulting in some serious back injuries. Honestly, the dude has never been the same."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Presidential Intervention and Cover-up (1997)
facts.body: Following the incident where U2's security chief was run over, President Zedillo personally called U2, requesting they not go to the press and instead come to the palace to discuss the matter. At the meeting, the President suggested "forget about what happened," effectively using his authority to prevent the story from becoming public. "So the next day, everybody from the van found themselves in the president's office. The sons were there too. With all the albums, they expected to be signed. Zidio said, look, let's forget about what happened. It's going to been a lot worse. You took on our secret service. Best let it go."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Creative Crisis (Post-Pop Album 1997)
facts.body: Following the critical and commercial failure of their 1997 album 'Pop', U2 experienced a significant creative crisis, forcing them to seek a new direction and sound. The band was under immense pressure from rock fans and critics who implored them to "save rock for the world." "The result was a creative crisis within the U2 organization. They desperately needed a course correction."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 00's Part 3: The Return of Rock
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Return to Rock Roots (Post-1997)
facts.body: Following the perceived failure of their `Pop` album in 1997, the band consciously decided to "go back to doing what they did best. Being a rock band," which led to the successful `All That You Can't Leave Behind`. "That's why they went back to doing what they did best. Being a rock band, that's what they were, why deny it."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Anthony Kiedis's "Last Chance" Rehab (1997)
facts.body: A trip to India sparked a spiritual awakening for Anthony Kiedis. Upon returning to Los Angeles in 1997, he checked into a "last chance" rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month, a facility known for hosting members of Mötley Crüe and Brent Gerowicz of Bad Religion. This visit initially seemed successful. "A trip to India put him in a spiritual place, and when he got back to LA, he checked into a last chance rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: Anthony Kiedis's Motorcycle Accident and Painkiller Addiction (1997)
facts.body: Following a severe motorcycle accident, Anthony Kiedis was prescribed Codeine, Percocet, and OxyContin. Due to his developed tolerance to chemicals, these medications were ineffective against the pain of nine months of physical rehabilitation for a shattered arm. On his 35th birthday, November 1, 1997, he checked into a rehab unit called Steps, but this attempt was also unsuccessful. "The pain of nine months of physical rehab for a shattered arm were extremely painful."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

Upon returning to Los Angeles in 1997, he checked into a "last chance" rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month, a facility known for hosting members of Mötley Crüe and Brent Gerowicz of Bad Religion. This visit initially seemed successful. "A trip to India put him in a spiritual place, and when he got back to LA, he checked into a last chance rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: Anthony Kiedis's Motorcycle Accident and Painkiller Addiction (1997)
facts.body: Following a severe motorcycle accident, Anthony Kiedis was prescribed Codeine, Percocet, and OxyContin. Due to his developed tolerance to chemicals, these medications were ineffective against the pain of nine months of physical rehabilitation for a shattered arm. On his 35th birthday, November 1, 1997, he checked into a rehab unit called Steps, but this attempt was also unsuccessful. "The pain of nine months of physical rehab for a shattered arm were extremely painful."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Red Hot Chili Peppers

facts.title: Long-Term Recovery and Current Status (1997-Present)
facts.body: Depeche Mode eventually overcame the tumultuous period between 1991 and 1997. Dave Gahan and Martin Gore are now sober, and Alan Wilder is living a quiet life. While Andy Fletcher died in 2022, Martin Gore and Dave Gahan continue to record and tour together, showing intent to move forward almost 50 years after the band's formation. "The good news is that the Pesh mode eventually came out on the other side of all things that happened between 1991 and 1997."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Glastonbury 1997 Performance Issues
facts.body: Radiohead's set at Glastonbury Festival on June 28, 1997, considered by some to be the "best show of all time," was initially fraught with technical difficulties. Halfway through their set, the band couldn't hear their stage monitors, leading to missed cues and frustration, almost causing them to walk off stage. To exacerbate matters, a roadie's spotlight kept blinding Thom Yorke. Yorke requested the lighting be turned onto the crowd, which coincided with the monitor problems clearing up and the "magic" setting in, solidifying their legend. "The group couldn't hear their stage monitors, and everyone started missing their cues. Frustration set in, and it looked for a while that Radiohead was going to cut things short and just walk off stage."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Radiohead

facts.title: Saturday Night Live Performance (March 27, 1997)
facts.body: The Tragically Hip appeared as a special musical guest on Saturday Night Live on March 27, 1997, performing two songs, including "Nautical Disaster." This high-profile national US television exposure was facilitated by Kingston native Dan Aykroyd, who was seen wearing a Tragically Hip t-shirt in the 1992 movie *Sneakers*. Despite this major vehicle, the performance did not result in a significant breakthrough in the American market. "That was one of two songs they performed on Saturday Night Live on March 27th, 1997. ... The answer is Dan Acroid. Dan is from Kingston. In fact, if you go back to the movie Sneakers with Acroid and Robert Redford and Ben Kingsley, Sydney Ponce, and River Phoenix in 1992, you'll see Dan wearing a tragically hip t-shirt under a sport coat."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: First Gig (August 14, 1997)
facts.body: The White Stripes' first public performance took place at The Gold Dollar, a bar in Detroit, on August 14, 1997. This marked their entry into the Detroit and Michigan underground indie scene, which connected them to "Motor City ancestors" like The Stooges and MC5. "And the date for that was August 14, 1997."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock
facts.name: The White Stripes

facts.title: Meg White's Introduction to Drums (July 14, 1997)
facts.body: Meg White, who had no prior drumming experience, unexpectedly sat down at Jack's drum kit at home on July 14, 1997, and began playing. Jack described this impromptu drumming as "liberating and refreshing," leading him to suggest forming a band with her. "Jack had his drum kit set up at home and Meg suddenly decided to sit down and started bashing away. She had no idea what she was doing because she had no experience on the drums whatsoever. But I quote Jack, When she started to play the drums with me just on a lark, it felt liberating and refreshing. There was something in it that opened me up."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The White Stripes

facts.title: First Gig (August 14, 1997)
facts.body: The White Stripes performed their first public concert on August 14, 1997, at the Gold Dollar Bar in Detroit, which was approximately three weeks after Meg first learned to play the drums. "Their first gig was at a place called the Gold Dollar Bar Detroit on August 14, 1997, which was about three weeks after Meg first learned how to play."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The White Stripes

facts.title: Formation and Early Releases (1997-1998)
facts.body: Jack and Meg White began performing in 1997 and started releasing singles in 1998, utilizing various independent labels that were willing to sign them. "Jack and Meg White first started hacking about in 1997 and releasing singles in 1998. They used a variety of indie labels. Whoever would have them, basically."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The White Stripes

facts.title: End of an Era (1997)
facts.body: By the end of 1997, everyone was distancing themselves from Britpop, the party was over, and the public and media were bored. The wave had run its course, precisely around the predicted six-year mark, with the Spice Girls and "girl power" becoming the new cultural drivers. "By the time the year was over, everybody was distancing themselves from anything to do with Britpop."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Britpop

facts.title: "Dirty Word" by End of 1997
facts.body: By the end of 1997, Britpop became "pretty much a dirty word" from which artists distanced themselves, as the original audience had grown up and moved on. This period was also marked by increased drug use, particularly heroin, which led to fragmentation. "And by the end of 1997, Britpop was pretty much a dirty word from which everyone distanced themselves."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12
facts.name: Britpop

facts.title: Official End (1997)
facts.body: By the end of 1997, Britpop was "officially over," with most artists distancing themselves from the genre due to a "bad hangover," the toll of drug use, and public/media boredom. Its influence would live on, but the wave had passed, consistent with the typical six-year cycle of cultural storms. "By the time the year was over, almost everyone was distancing themselves from anything to do with Britpop. The party was officially over."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop
facts.name: Britpop

facts.title: Decline and End (Circa 1997)
facts.body: The Britpop movement began to die around 1997. This period saw key bands like Blur starting to abandon the genre and pursue entirely different musical directions, signaling the end of Britpop's dominant era.
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.name: Britpop

facts.title: Decline of Britpop (1997)
facts.body: By 1997, the Britpop genre was in sharp decline, with its purist form losing relevance. Many bands, including Pulp, were actively experimenting with new sounds like hardcore and lofi, while others were disbanding, making it a challenging period for acts rooted in traditional Britpop. "ya 1997, malamente era época para Britpop y menos aún para ese Britpop tan purista."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan

facts.title: David Bowie's Incorporation (1997)
facts.body: Techno was among the new genres of dance music that David Bowie explored and integrated into his 1997 album, *Earthling*. His adoption of the genre was interpreted by some as an official endorsement from a major artist. "He'd become interested in various new genres of dance music, including industrial, techno, jungle, and drum and bass."

facts.title: Taylor Hawkins Joins the Band (1997)
facts.body: On March 18, 1997, it was officially announced that Taylor Hawkins was joining the Foo Fighters. He transitioned from being the drummer for Alanis Morissette, who at the time was a bigger act, to an up-and-coming rock band featuring the former Nirvana drummer, Dave Grohl. "So on March 18th, 1997, it was announced that Taylor was officially a food fighter."

facts.title: Breakup and Temporary Hiatus (1997)
facts.body: Following the Toronto show in 1997, three-quarters of the band parted ways with Scott Weiland due to his ongoing personal struggles with drugs, legal issues, and domestic problems. This was acknowledged as a necessary break for everyone to sort things out creatively, musically, physically, mentally, and legally, though not necessarily permanent. "Following the show, three quarters of the band and Wyland parted ways."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Stone Temple Pilots

facts.title: Post-Tour Cancellations (January 1997)
facts.body: Following a successful six-week tour, Stone Temple Pilots canceled a New Year's show in Anchorage, Alaska, without explanation, and two subsequent shows in Hawaii for the first week of January 1997, disappointing over 30,000 fans. "Then two more shows scheduled for the first week in January and Hawaii were also blown out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Stone Temple Pilots

facts.title: Manager's Statement on Scott's Relapse (January 6, 1997)
facts.body: On January 6, 1997, STP's manager Steve Stewart issued a statement confirming Scott Wyland was having problems again and was seeking care, but assured that he was safe, not arrested, and the band remained together. "Scott has made the band aware that he was having problems again and is taking care of himself at this point."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Stone Temple Pilots

facts.title: Impact of Scott's Relapse on Album Charts (January 1997)
facts.body: Scott Wyland's relapse and subsequent undetermined rehab stay came at a time when "Tiny Music" had significantly climbed the album charts, jumping 78 spots in a month due to the recent tour, causing frustration for the other band members. "Tiny music had jumped 78 spots on the album charts in a month because of the tour."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Stone Temple Pilots

facts.title: Rumors of Disbandment (May 25, 1997)
facts.body: After a show in Toronto on May 25, 1997, rumors began to circulate that Stone Temple Pilots were "finished for good." "After a show in Toronto on May 25th, 1997, the rumors were that the Stone Temple pilots were finished for good."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Secretive Battle with Addiction (1997-1999)
facts.body: Reznor first tried to address his addiction in 1997, keeping it secretive due to shame. He struggled through the recording of "The Fragile" on a "pretty slippery slope." "I had addressed the situation in 97 and was secretive about it and didn't want anyone to know because I felt very shame that I'd let something get out of hand."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nine Inch Nails

facts.title: Plagiarism Lawsuit by Mark Anofrio (1997-1998)
facts.body: On August 18, 1997, Trent Reznor was sued by LA musician Mark Anofrio, who alleged that six of his songs, recorded under the name Elephant Man, were stolen. Anofrio claimed he sent a tape to Reznor after an internet chat session. Five songs from "The Downward Spiral" (1994) and "Burn" from the "Natural Born Killers" soundtrack were identified as alleged ripoffs. The case eventually went before a federal judge on December 1, 1998, and was dismissed. "On August 18th, 1997, he was notified that an LA musician named Mark Anofrio had accused Trent of stealing six of his songs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nine Inch Nails

facts.title: "Dark Time" After Britpop - 1997
facts.body: The end of Britpop in 1997 marked the beginning of a "dark time" for Alt Rock, despite many good years in the early 90s, with "rock is dead" cries becoming prevalent. "No one really wanted to admit it in 1997, but after so many good years, it was the beginning of a dark time for Alt Rock."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

facts.body: By 1997, Damon Albarn underwent a "stunning aesthetic reversal," shifting his musical interests from proudly British pop (anti-grunge) to low-fi American alternative bands (Pavement, The Pixies), obscure 1970s German progressive rock, and Sub-Saharan African music. He also began spending more time in Iceland, manifesting this change in Blur's self-titled 1997 album. "Damon had become fascinated by low-fi American alternative music from bands like Pavement and The Pixies. He was also getting deeper into obscure German progressive rock from the 1970s and several forms of music from sub-Saharan Africa."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop
facts.name: Blur

facts.title: David Bowie's Incorporation (1997)
facts.body: Industrial music was one of the new dance genres that David Bowie became interested in and incorporated into his 1997 album, *Earthling*. This was seen by some as Bowie giving his official recognition to the genre. "He'd become interested in various new genres of dance music, including industrial, techno, jungle, and drum and bass."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Plagiarism Suit by Mark Anofrio (1997-1998)
facts.body: Trent Reznor was accused by LA musician Mark Anofrio on August 18, 1997, of stealing six songs, including five from "The Downward Spiral" (1994) and "Burn." Anofrio claimed he had sent recorded material, under the name Elephant Man, to Reznor's home. The case, after delays and Anofrio dropping claims on some songs, was eventually dismissed by a federal judge on December 1, 1998. "On August 18th, 1997, he was notified that an LA musician named Mark Anofrio had accused Trent of stealing six of his songs."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: EMI's Composition of Bach-Style Music (1997)
facts.body: At a 1997 University of Oregon competition, the computer program EMI (Experiments in Musical Intelligence), developed by David Cope, composed pieces in the style of classical composer J.S. Bach. While music experts could discern it was computer-generated, they believed the program had played an actual Bach composition, demonstrating its sophisticated mimicry. "One was by a computer called EMI, which was given information on the musical style of classical composer J.S. Bach."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

facts.title: Be Here Now Production (1997)
facts.body: During the recording of *Be Here Now* in 1997, Noel, under the influence of cocaine, insisted on making the record sound "bigger and louder" by layering numerous guitars and turning up the high end, a perception he later attributed to his drug use. "Noel kept wanting to make the record sound bigger and louder. So he insisted on layer after layer after layer of guitars. And he wanted the high end turned up because he didn't think there was enough."

facts.title: Around the World (1997) – Goal Was to Sound Like Chic; Repeated 144 Times; Declared One of the Most Repetitive Songs Ever
facts.body: "Around the World" was designed to sound like Chic (Nile Rodgers's disco-era band). The song has five instruments and a robotic voice saying "Around the World." In the original version, the phrase is repeated 144 times (80 times in the short edit). A scientific analysis of music declared it one of the most repetitive songs ever released — and that is its genius, as repetition is what creates the sensation of losing yourself in music. "A scientific analysis of music declared this to be one of the most repetitive songs ever released. And that is its genius."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Daft Punk

facts.title: Soundgarden Breakup (1997) – Tension from Manager/Wife Susan Silver and Separate Tour Transport
facts.body: The band broke up in 1997 partly due to the unresolvable conflict of interest created by Cornell being married to Susan Silver, who was also the band's manager (and the manager of Alice in Chains and Screaming Trees). By the end of the band's existence, each member was reportedly traveling separately by their own bus or plane between shows. After the divorce in 2002, Cornell filed a complaint with the California Labor Commission in 2006 alleging Silver had performed booking work without the required talent agent's license, and sought return of money she made from Soundgarden activities in 2005. "No conflict of interest there."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Chris Cornell

"Allison Chains guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit that Lane used once in a while, but mostly he just painted, watched TV, played video games, and did drugs."

facts.title: David Bowie's Incorporation (1997)
facts.body: Jungle music was one of the contemporary dance genres that captured David Bowie's interest and was subsequently featured on his 1997 album, *Earthling*. This artistic choice was viewed by some as an important recognition of the genre by a mainstream artist. "He'd become interested in various new genres of dance music, including industrial, techno, jungle, and drum and bass."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Jungle

facts.title: Keith Flint's Creative Involvement (1997)
facts.body: Prior to 1997, Keith Flint was primarily a "figurehead" in The Prodigy, not involved in the creative process, a common arrangement in some bands. However, for "The Fat of the Land" (1997), he began working creatively with Liam Howlett, introducing a more punk and rock-influenced sound with distorted guitars and ska influences, which significantly evolved the band's music and visual iconography. "Keith Flint until 1997 was within The Prodigy but was mostly a figurehead... but precisely on this album, The Fat of the Land, Keith Flint began to work within the creative process of the album together with Liam Howlett."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia
facts.name: The Prodigy

facts.title: Cultural Impact of "The Fat of the Land" (1997)
facts.body: "The Fat of the Land" was described as the album of an "angry generation" who had not experienced punk and found grunge a bit outdated. It became a global phenomenon, selling millions, with its t-shirts ubiquitous despite widespread radio censorship and controversial music videos. The album caused a "true commotion" and was embraced by many. "The Fat of the Land is the electronic punk album par excellence and it was the album of a generation."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: The Prodigy: Electrónica y rabia que hizo historia

facts.title: Death (November 22–23, 1997) – Ritz Carlton Sydney, Belt, No Suicide Note; Coroner: Consistent with Auto-Erotic Asphyxiation
facts.body: The night before Michael Hutchence's death began normally: a dinner with his father and stepmother at a restaurant called the Flapper of India, where he seemed fine. He returned to room 524 at the Ritz Carlton Double Bay, Sydney. Ex-girlfriend Kim Wilson (inspiration for "Suicide Blonde") came to the hotel with her boyfriend; they drank daiquiris, champagne, and beer in the bar before going to Hutchence's room. They left around 4am. Over the following hours, Hutchence made multiple calls but reached only answering machines. Early that morning he went downstairs looking disheveled to mail some letters — the last time anyone saw him alive. A maid found his body around noon on Saturday, November 23. He appeared to have gone into a violent rage — prescription pills scattered across the room, a broken hand from hitting the wall, facial cuts, furniture thrown — before fastening a leather belt to the bathroom door and hanging himself. There was no suicide note. The official coroner's verdict was death consistent with auto-erotic asphyxiation, a practice that kills an estimated 500 to 1,000 people per year worldwide. Hutchence had acknowledged in a late interview trying to achieve "the ultimate sexual high," and his mother confirmed he had spent time with sadomasochists in the preceding months. "The coroner says is consistent with auto-erotic asphyxiation, a death by misadventure."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: New Record Deal and Album (1997)
facts.body: At the start of 1997, InXS secured a new record deal and had an album in production, signaling their intent for a professional "fresh start." "By the beginning of 1997, in excess had a new record deal and a new album on the way. Professionally, the group was looking for a fresh start."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: 20th Anniversary TV Special (1997)
facts.body: In November and December 1997, InXS was in Sydney filming a TV special for Australian television to commemorate their 20th anniversary, coinciding with local performance dates. "In excess was back home in Sydney, filming a TV special for Australian TV. Everybody was pumped up for this documentary commemorating the 20th anniversary of In Excess, which coincided with some dates at home in November and December."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: Decline in Late 1990s and 20th Anniversary Special (1997)
facts.body: By the late 1990s, the "best days" of INXS were considered to be behind them, although they remained a profitable concern. On November 22, 1997, the band was in Sydney, Australia, working on a TV special to commemorate their 20th anniversary. "By the late 90s, the best days of InXS were behind them, but they were still very much a profitable concern."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: Relationship Turmoil and Self-Medication (November 1997)
facts.body: Michael Hutchence was experiencing intense personal turmoil due to his relationship with UK TV presenter Paula Yates, the ex-wife of Bob Geldof, especially concerning a dispute over children. He was described as not being in a good place and was self-medicating with drugs, including heroin, which he and Paula were both using. "The turmoil with Paula and Bob was peaking over children. She was expecting. He was self-medicating."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: Last Public Sightings and Communications (November 1997)
facts.body: On the night of Friday, November 21, 1997, Michael Hutchence had an Indian dinner with his father and stepmother, appearing to have a good time despite his father's unease. He returned to Room 524 at the Ritz Carlton Hotel in Sydney around 10:30 PM, joking with girls in the elevator. He then went on a "last bender," making calls to former girlfriends Kim Wilson (who visited with her current boyfriend until 4 AM) and Michelle Bennett (who rushed to the hotel after a worried call but found no answer). He also had two calls with Bob Geldof around 5 AM about a court injunction, including a loud 20-minute argument, and a desperate-sounding call with Paula Yates at 5:38 AM. His last sighting was asking a front desk clerk to mail two letters—one to Paula and one to a friend in Hong Kong. "Sometime after that, Michael went down to the front desk and asked the clerk to mail two letters, one to Paula and the other to a friend in Hong Kong. That was the last time anyone saw him alive."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: Suicide (November 1997)
facts.body: Between 9:55 AM and 10:30 AM on Saturday, November 22, 1997, Michael Hutchence, depressed, drunk, and sleep-deprived, entered a violent rage, throwing furniture, punching a wall, breaking his hand, and scattering five different prescription pills. He then hanged himself with a leather snakeskin belt from a doorknob in his hotel room. A housekeeper discovered his body at 11:50 AM. No suicide note was found. "depressed, drunk, and sleep deprived, Michael had gone into a violent rage, throwing furniture around, breaking his hand, punching a wall, and scattering five different prescription pills all over the place. Sometime between 955 AM and 1030 AM, he hanged himself with a leather snake skin belt from a doorknob."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: INXS

facts.title: Jarvis Cocker's Cocaine Addiction (1997)
facts.body: In 1997, Jarvis Cocker struggled with a severe cocaine addiction, which significantly impacted the band's performances and creative output. Recordings from their concerts that year show some to be "truly pathetic," with anecdotes like Jarvis Cocker vomiting on stage in Spain. This addiction also contributed to a creative block, where he struggled to write new material after "Different Class." "a serious problem was the addition to cocaine by Jarvis Cocker that caused during a year, well, there are recordings of the concerts in 1997 of Palt that some are truly pathetic."

facts.title: Raine Maida's Intervention in Labatt's Standoff (c. 1997)
facts.body: During a standoff at a festival in Manitoba (part of the "Trusted by Millions" tour, around 1997-1998) over a Labatt's balloon on stage, Raine Maida, the singer from Our Lady Peace, intervened. He explained 5440's contractual clauses to the promoters, resulting in the balloon being deflated, allowing 5440 to perform. "thanks to him, they took it down."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Securing a Deal with Sony Music Canada (c. 1997)
facts.body: Sony Music Canada, under the leadership of Paul Berger and A&R representative Richard Zuckerman, became interested in 5440 as it sought to grow. This led to a new record deal for the band, though without an accompanying American contract. "Paul Berger was brought in to run the company. And he was eager to find stuff. And somebody mentioned us to him and Richard Zuckerman, who was his A&R guy."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Death at Ritz Carlton (November 22-23, 1997)
facts.body: Michael Hutchence met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia. On the night of November 22nd, 1997, after filming a TV special for INXS's 20th anniversary and having dinner, he returned to his suite. Following late-night visitors, he made phone calls, then appeared "really rough" at the front desk. Back in his room, he apparently went into a rage, trashing the room, throwing prescription pills, and breaking his hand. Sometime between 9:50 am and 10:30 am on November 23rd, 1997, he fastened a leather belt to a doorknob and hanged himself. He was found by a maid at 11:50 am. The most popular verdict was auto-erotic asphyxiation, and he was 37 years old. "Michael Hutchins met his end in room 524 of the Ritz Carlton in Sydney, Australia."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Michael Hutchence

facts.title: Death by Apparent Suicide (November 22, 1997)
facts.body: Michael Hutchence was found dead in a Sydney hotel room on November 22, 1997, in what was apparently a suicide. Those close to him believe his death was ultimately a consequence of the brain injury he suffered five years prior in Copenhagen. "on November 22, 1997, Hutchins was found dead in a Sydney hotel room, apparently by suicide."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Michael Hutchence

facts.title: Death at Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel (November 22-23, 1997)
facts.body: Michael Hutchence's final hours began after dinner with his father and stepmother in Sydney on November 22, 1997, where he subsequently returned to room 524 at the Ritz Carlton Double Bay Hotel. He had champagne, daiquiris, and beer with his ex-girlfriend Kim Wilson and her current boyfriend in the hotel bar, continuing to his room for a nightcap. After they left at 4 AM, he made several unanswered phone calls to ex-girlfriends. Early on November 23rd, he mailed some letters, appearing "pretty rough" to the clerk. Housekeeping discovered him dead around noon, the room in disarray with prescription pills scattered and furniture moved. He died between 9:50 and 10:30 AM, having been strangled by a belt hung on a door. His cause of death has been debated, with official findings concluding auto-erotic asphyxiation, though suicide was also considered, despite no note. "Michael was dead. He had been strangled by a belt hung on a door."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Michael Hutchence
